# Dark mode, finally

Dark mode ships today in Margin 3.4, on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android. Flip it on under Settings → Appearance, or leave it on Auto and it follows your system clock.

People have been asking since 2023. We should say why it took this long.

The first attempt was working a year ago. Invert the palette, ship it, go home. It looked awful. Notes are mostly small text, and pure white on pure black smears at 14px — the letterforms bloom into each other on OLED screens especially. So we landed on #E8E6E3 on #1A1A1A, which measures 13.2:1 and stops the halo.

Then the highlighter. All five colors were picked against a white page, and on a dark background the yellow one lit up like a road sign. Each one is retuned, and old highlights convert on the fly, so a note you marked up in 2024 opens looking the way you meant it to.

Two more things worth knowing. Images and PDFs stay at full brightness instead of getting dimmed, because a dimmed screenshot is an unreadable screenshot. And code blocks get their own syntax theme rather than a recolored version of the light one.

If something looks wrong — a plugin with hardcoded colors, a theme that fights the new tokens — send it to support@margin.app with a screenshot. We're watching that inbox closely this week.

Update from the App Store, Play Store, or Help → Check for Updates.

# Dark mode, at last

Dark mode arrives today in Margin 3.4, on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android. Turn it on in Settings → Appearance, or leave it on Auto and it tracks your system clock.

The requests started in 2023. It seems fair to explain the delay.

We had a version running a year ago. Flip the palette, ship it, done. It read badly. Notes are mostly small text, and white on black smears at 14px; the letterforms bleed into each other, worst of all on OLED. What we shipped instead is #E8E6E3 on #1A1A1A, which measures 13.2:1 and kills the halo.

Then there was the highlighter. All five colors were chosen against a white page, and against a dark one the yellow glowed like a traffic sign. Every color is retuned, and existing highlights convert as the file opens, so a note you marked up in 2024 still looks like what you intended.

Two other details. Images and PDFs keep their full brightness rather than getting dimmed, since a dimmed screenshot is a screenshot nobody can read. And code blocks get a purpose-built syntax theme instead of the light one with its colors swapped.

If anything looks off, whether it's a plugin with hardcoded colors or a theme that fights the new tokens, mail support@margin.app with a screenshot. Someone is reading that inbox all week.
